description: The map of the UBL example world: routes, towns and villages, the offshore platform and the pipelines' metering stations, on a grid of 256 x 192 squares of 3.5 km (tools/world_model.py, GRID). tools/world_model.py builds the tile model from it, from the parties and from the terrain (world/terrain.json: land, sea, river, estuary, land cover, countries and heights, made by tools/terrain.py from world/terrain-inputs.json, O152). Stations are the pipelines' border metering stations. Towns and localities (villages) give their population (for the villages the decided range) and the width of their built-up area in km (built_km, owner 2026-11-18, O92): the model draws a built-up area of that size around the centre c. Localities give the parties outside the towns a place in their address. Villages (O152, owner 2026-11-18; on the map only: no parties, no documents) fill the land between the towns: each with its square c, country, region, founded, why (the reason for its site), lives_on, its population band and the width of its built-up area, and its way of farming ("farming"); the larger ones have a name ("names" per language: in Urvania the English (Italian) name and the Urvanian one, made by tools/lexicon.py from the word in "name_from"; on Lisavu the Lisavan one, with an English name where settlers named the place; in Bayvarra English settler names), the others are unnamed. They are sited by analysis/world-position/site_villages.py and joined to the roads by minor roads ("village-<i>-<j>", tools/lay_routes.py). A town or village farms the land within its reach in its way of farming ("farming", a town's reach "farm_km"); tools/land_use.py turns this into the land use the model and both maps draw. A town's districts ("districts") trace its growth: each with a name, a period ("periods" names them), the years, its character (core, administration, residential, suburb, industry, port), its centre ("at", in squares) and its relative size ("r_km"): the model grows the built-up area as the union of the districts to the decided size. A town may have a harbour of its own (a quay square and the side its water lies on), without a party: Larkmouth's. Roads, rails and pipelines are given square by square, each square a neighbour of the last, diagonals included, as tools/lay_routes.py laid them over the terrain (O152 stage 3: least-cost ways with the gradient of their class, a main road about 6 to 7 %, a minor road up to 10 %, a railway 1.5 to 2 %, following the valleys and crossing ridges at their passes; tools/routing.py): a road's "class" is main or minor, "bridges" and "tunnels" list the squares a route spans or runs under; the access roads to the parties are routes too ("access-<party>"). Do not edit these by hand: change the network in tools/lay_routes.py and run it. The river route names the barges' first quay, and the model follows the river's squares from there to the estuary, below the rapids above Ferrano. The drawn map is a diagram (O82): it may stretch distances, and Lisavu, about 1,000 km east of Lumeport, is drawn nearer, in its own part of the grid with open sea all round, as an inset. Quarters ("quarters") are composite buildings that several parties share on one square: each with its id, name, kind, square (at), the street it opens on (a road route's id), the number of wings it has room for (room) and its occupants (wings, a party id each, in the order of the wings: the two halves of the back wing, then the side wings from the back to the front); every party standing on the square is one of them.

wiki.title: Ore line
wiki.short: Railway in Urvania from the mine to the works at Ferrano
wiki.lead: The **Ore line** is a railway in [[Urvania]] that carries iron ore from the mine on the lower flank of the massif down to the works at [[Ferrano]]. It is about 166 km long.

sections.title: Route
sections.text: The line starts at the mine's siding at Fucinalta, where the wagons are loaded and weighed at the mine's portal, and follows the valleys down to Ferrano, keeping to gradients of at most 2 %. Its river bridge stands 78 m above the water.

sections.title: Operation
sections.text: The tracks belong to the [[Rail Infrastructure Agency of Urvania]], which allocates the train paths and dispatches every train; [[Ferrano Rail Cargo]] runs the ore trains.

wiki.title: Ferrano–Marrowdale line
wiki.short: Railway from Ferrano across the border to Marrowdale
wiki.lead: The **Ferrano–Marrowdale line** is the railway from [[Ferrano]] across the border to [[Marrowdale]], the main rail link between [[Urvania]] and [[Bayvarra]].

sections.title: Operation
sections.text: Container trains run from the intermodal hub at Ferrano past the border to the distribution centre's siding at Marrowdale. On the Urvanian side the [[Rail Infrastructure Agency of Urvania]] owns the tracks up to the border station.

wiki.short: Weekly container service between Lumeport and Lisavu
wiki.lead: The **Lumeport–Selanu shipping service** links [[Lumeport]] and [[Selanu]] by container ship. [[Tidewell Ocean Lines]] was founded in 1974 to run it, under the Lumeport Agreement between [[Bayvarra]] and [[Lisavu]].

sections.title: Route
sections.text: The ships sail out through the estuary and the bay and round the island's south-eastern cape to the lee side, about 1,200 km, in about 48 hours at 13.5 knots.

wiki.title: Lumeport–Selanu air cargo route
wiki.short: Air cargo route between Lumeport and Lisavu
wiki.lead: The **Lumeport–Selanu air cargo route** links the airports of [[Lumeport]] and [[Selanu]], about 1,080 km apart. [[Kelaro Air Cargo]], the island's airline, flies it with a freighter.

sections.title: Operation
sections.text: The flight takes about two and a half hours from gate to gate in still air; the timetable allows 2 h 45 eastbound and 3 h 00 westbound, for the westerly winds and delays.

wiki.title: Kelpstone–Ferrano gas pipeline
wiki.short: Gas pipeline from Bayvarra's north coast to Urvania
wiki.lead: The **Kelpstone–Ferrano gas pipeline** carries natural gas from the gas plant of [[Kelpstone Gas]] near Gullhaven, on [[Bayvarra]]'s north coast, across the border to the power station near [[Serravona]] in [[Urvania]]. It has carried gas since 2011.

sections.title: Route
sections.text: The gas comes ashore from an offshore field by a subsea line of about 83 km, from the production platform to the plant of [[Kelpstone Gas]] near Gullhaven. From the plant the pipeline runs about 207 km to [[Montebrio Power]]; a branch of about 97 km leads to the city gate of [[Ferrano Grid]]. A metering station on Bayvarra's side of the border measures the gas that crosses into Urvania.

wiki.title: Wool line
wiki.short: Railway from Marrowdale to the harbour of Larkmouth
wiki.lead: The **Wool line** is the railway from [[Marrowdale]] down to the harbour of [[Larkmouth]], in [[Bayvarra]]. It was built for the wool of the plateau and the dry east.

sections.title: History
sections.text: Bayvarra built its railways in the late 19th century, and villages grew at the stations. From the 1880s wool stores and sale rooms lined the line's last stretch to Larkmouth's harbour.

districts.name: Ruldraz (the old town)
districts.note: The Urvanian town on the terrace of the north bank where the northern valley meets the river below the rapids: its lanes, the market and the old bridgehead.

districts.name: Borgo Toscano
districts.note: The Tuscan trading post of 1609-10 by the landing at the foot of the rapids: a walled warehouse court and a chapel; the river quays grew from it.

districts.name: Città Nuova
districts.note: The Sardinian and then Italian new town on the higher terrace north of the old town: a grid of streets, the residency, the barracks, the churches and the arcaded main street.

districts.name: Scalo
districts.note: The railway station, its yards and the first works beside the line north of the centre (the iron foundry, later the bench works).

districts.name: Villaggio Inglese
districts.note: The garden suburb of the British administration's officials and families on the hill north-west of the centre.

districts.name: Zona Industriale
districts.note: Industry and logistics along the railway east of the centre: the works, the intermodal hub, the depots and warehouses of the protected economy and of the Accord's trade.

districts.name: Borgo Nord
districts.note: Flats and houses along the road north, up the valley.

districts.name: Oltreponte
districts.note: The suburb across the river bridge, along the road south.

districts.name: Quartiere Est
districts.note: Housing along the main road east, towards the border.

wiki.short: Capital of Urvania
wiki.lead: **Ferrano** (Urvanian *Ruldraz*) is the capital of [[Urvania]], with about {population} people. It stands where the northern valley meets the main river, just below the rapids that end navigation: the country's works, its rail hub and its river port.

sections.title: Geography
sections.text: The town lies on the terraces of the north bank, at the foot of the rapids, where the barges of the lower river turn. A road bridge, about 106 m above the river, links the farmland south of the river with the town; the suburb of Oltreponte grew beyond it. The railway runs north up the valley towards the mine and east towards the border with [[Bayvarra]].

sections.title: History
sections.text: Ruldraz was the Urvanians' town before the Europeans came: its lanes, market and old bridgehead are the old town. A Tuscan trading post of 1609–10 at the landing below the rapids left the walled warehouse court of Borgo Toscano. From 1840 the Sardinian and then Italian protectorate laid out Città Nuova on the higher terrace, and the railway and the first works came in the 1880s. The British administration of 1941 to 1962 added a garden suburb; after independence the town grew along its roads and its railway, with the works and depots of the protected economy and of the Accord.

districts.name: Old Town
districts.note: The settlers' company town of about 1840 by the mouth of the brook (its first fresh water) on the shore of the bay, commanding the narrows.

districts.name: Government Hill
districts.note: The colonial capital's government buildings, churches and banks on the rise south of the old town.

districts.name: Dockside
districts.note: The deep-water quays, warehouses and the railway to them, at the inner basin behind the narrows.

districts.name: Brookside
districts.note: Workers' terraces up the brook west of the old town.

districts.name: Northshore
districts.note: Houses along the coast road north.

districts.name: Westside
districts.note: Works on the estuary shore west of the centre: the water works, the packaging works.

districts.name: Mill Quarter
districts.note: The textile mill of 1976, built to spin the island's duty-free cotton, and the trades around it.

districts.name: Riverside
districts.note: Newer housing on the estuary shore between the works and the docks.

wiki.short: Capital and port city of Bayvarra
wiki.lead: **Lumeport** is the capital and port city of [[Bayvarra]], with about {population} people, on a bay at the narrows of the estuary. It gave its name to the [[Lumeport Trade Accord]], signed there in 1994, and is the seat of its council.

sections.title: Geography
sections.text: The town stands on the shore of the bay where the estuary of the [[Runmek]] narrows before it opens to the sea; the narrows command the entry to the river. A brook from the low hills west of the centre runs through the town to the bay and gave it its first fresh water. The deep-water quays lie at the inner basin behind the narrows.

sections.title: History
sections.text: In the late 1830s the settlers' company kept a trading station at the narrows. When Britain annexed the coast on 29 November 1841 it fortified the station and laid out the town as the colony's seat, and as the river trade grew Lumeport took over from [[Larkmouth]] as capital in 1852. Government Hill gained its government buildings, churches and banks in the 19th century, and the deep-water quays and their railway came between the 1870s and 1914. The Lumeport Agreement of 1974 brought the textile mill of 1976, built to spin the island's duty-free cotton.

towns.name: Marrowdale
towns.note: An inland town in Upland State, near the border: the distributor with its rail siding, the sawmill, the furniture maker and the engineering works.

districts.name: Market Square
districts.note: The drovers' market and wool sales at the stream crossing on the road down from the plateau: the town's square, inns and stores.

districts.name: Railway End
districts.note: The station yard and the sawmill by the railway.

districts.name: Hill Street
districts.note: Villas on the slope north of the square.

districts.name: Eastgate
districts.note: Houses along the road east.

districts.name: Depot Road
districts.note: The distribution centre and the trades of the Accord by the railway east of the town.

wiki.short: Inland town in Upland State, Bayvarra
wiki.lead: **Marrowdale** is an inland town in Upland State, [[Bayvarra]], with about {population} people, near the border with [[Urvania]]. It grew from a drovers' market and is now a town of the railway and the timber trade.

sections.title: History
sections.text: The town began in the 1850s as the drovers' market and wool sales at the stream crossing on the road down from the plateau; on 12 April 1858 the plateau became a colony of its own, Upland, and since 1899 it is Upland State of [[Bayvarra]]. The railway came in the 1880s, and with it the station yard and the sawmill. After the Trade Accord entered into force, a distribution centre and the trades of the Accord settled by the railway east of the town.

sections.title: Economy
sections.text: Marrowdale lives from the railway and the timber of the Upland State Forest, which lies on the slope north of the town: the sawmill, a furniture maker, an engineering works and a distribution centre with its own siding.

districts.name: Selanu
districts.note: The Lisavan village on the sheltered bay of the east-south-east coast, which gave the town its name.

districts.name: Port Wrenfield
districts.note: The English settlers' town on the wharf north of the village: their street of stores and the customs house.

districts.name: Upper Town
districts.note: Offices, churches and houses on the rise behind the wharf.

districts.name: Agreement Quarter
districts.note: Warehouses, the brokers and the trades the Lumeport Agreement called into being.

districts.name: Hillside
districts.note: Houses on the slope south-west of the centre.

wiki.short: Capital and only town of Lisavu
wiki.lead: **Selanu** (English *Port Wrenfield*) is the capital and only town of [[Lisavu]], with about {population} people, on a sheltered bay of the island's east coast. It holds the island's port, and its airport lies on the plain to the north.

sections.title: History
sections.text: The Lisavan village on the bay gave the town its name; by about the 14th century it was the seat of the rulers of the whole island, whose meeting ground drew the elders of every village each spring. In the 19th century the English settlers built Port Wrenfield on the wharf north of the village, with its street of stores and its customs house, and offices, churches and houses rose on the slope behind the wharf. The Lumeport Agreement of 1974 brought the warehouses, brokers and trades of the Agreement Quarter.

towns.name: Larkmouth
towns.note: Bayvarra's first town and first capital (O153): the British settlers' landing of the 1820s at the mouth of the largest east-coast river, sheltered behind its headland, with fresh water and the dry grazing land behind it; a wool and meat port for the dry east. It has no parties: on the map and in the story only.

districts.name: The Landing
districts.note: Where the first settlers landed, behind the headland at the mouth of the east river: the old harbour and its stone quay.

districts.name: Capital Hill
districts.note: The first capital's Government House, church and court on the rise above the landing.

districts.name: Woolstores
districts.note: Wool stores and sale rooms along the wool line's last stretch to the harbour.

districts.name: Freezing Works
districts.note: The meat freezing works by the river mouth, for the frozen meat trade.

districts.name: North End
districts.note: Houses along the road north.

wiki.short: Port town on the east coast of Bayvarra, its first capital
wiki.lead: **Larkmouth** is a port town in Coastal State, [[Bayvarra]], with about {population} people, at the mouth of the [[River Lark|Lark]], the largest river of the east coast. It was the British settlers' first town and the colony's first capital.

sections.title: History
sections.text: The first settlers landed here on 16 February 1824, behind the headland at the mouth of the east river, where they found a sheltered harbour, fresh water and dry grazing land behind it. Their Government House, church and court stood on the rise above the landing until the capital moved to [[Lumeport]] in 1852. From the 1880s wool stores and sale rooms lined the wool line's last stretch to the harbour, and after 1914 a freezing works by the river mouth served the frozen meat trade.

sections.title: Economy
sections.text: Larkmouth is the wool and meat port of the dry east, at the end of the railway down from [[Marrowdale]].

localities.name: Serravona
localities.note: The mining village at the ore mine.

localities.name: Gullhaven
localities.note: A fishing village on Bayvarra's north coast, by the gas plant.

localities.name: Valico Euridice
localities.note: The Urvanian side of the road border crossing, named after Forte Euridice, the town 8 km down the road: the customs post, its truck park and a few houses of customs officers and forwarding agents In the municipality of Forte Euridice.

localities.name: Euridice Crossing
localities.note: The Bayvarran side of the road border crossing, known like the Urvanian side by the fort town across the border, as the crossing has been since the boundary convention: the customs post, its truck park and a few houses.

platforms.note: The gas field's production platform, offshore: it has no name or address in the documents, only its place in the world's map grid and its WGS 84 coordinates.

stations.note: The border metering station of the gas pipeline, on Bayvarra's side of the border: it measures the gas that crosses into Urvania.

quarters.name: Government Quarter
quarters.note: Lumeport's government quarter on Government Hill: one building in one style, its wings round a court that opens on Civic Square. Public bodies of Bayvarra and of Lumeport have their offices in it, each in a wing of its own, with its own entrance and address on Civic Square.

villages.name: Shinglebeck
villages.why: Where a stream comes down to a shingle shore of the north coast, on the coast road.
villages.lives_on: Sheep and fishing.

villages.name: Harrowmead
villages.why: On the plateau near the border, on a confluence in the wetter western part of Bayvarra.
villages.lives_on: The market of the western wheat land.

villages.name: Barleycombe
villages.why: In a valley of the western wheat land between Marrowdale and the border, where two streams meet.
villages.lives_on: The market of the western wheat land's barley, wheat and sheep farms.

villages.name: Tallowford
villages.why: On the north bank of the main river, where the drove road down the valley forded the second plateau river (about 5,500 km²) some 5 km above its mouth, about 40 km downstream of the border crossing and Forte Euridice; the main road to Marrowdale and the railway came later and pass beside it.
villages.lives_on: Its ford market and its farms: the stock sales, the grain store and the railway's stock yards of the wheat and sheep land around it.

villages.name: Wetherholme
villages.why: Where two rivers of the plateau meet, the homestead of one of the first sheep runs.
villages.lives_on: The market of the plateau's sheep runs and wheat farms.

villages.name: Ploverness
villages.why: On a low point of the north coast at a stream mouth.
villages.lives_on: Fishing and sheep.

villages.name: Brackenmere
villages.why: Between Marrowdale and Lumeport on the road and the railway, by a spring-fed pond (the mere) in bracken-covered ground: a stage on the road down to the capital.
villages.lives_on: Its station and the road, the farms round it, joinery for Marrowdale's furniture trade.

villages.name: Ewesbridge
villages.why: On the road north from Larkmouth over the dry east, at a bridge over a creek.
villages.lives_on: A sheep station's village: wool, the road.

villages.name: Wadebank
villages.why: On the north shore of Lumeport's bay, on the road north, where the shore shelves gently.
villages.lives_on: Oysters and fishing, market gardens for Lumeport, and its commuters.

villages.name: Drovers Halt
villages.why: On the coast road from Larkmouth to Lumeport, where it crosses a stream at a confluence: an inn where drovers rested their stock.
villages.lives_on: The coast road's trade, the farms and sheep runs behind it.

villages.name: Hartsedge
villages.why: At a station on the wool line between Marrowdale and Larkmouth, on the edge of a rise.
villages.lives_on: The station's stock yards and grain store, the sheep and cattle runs.

villages.name: Fleecewell
villages.why: Just south of Larkmouth on the coast road and the wool line, at a well where the flocks were watered and washed before shearing.
villages.lives_on: Shearing sheds and wool stores by the station, sheep runs.

villages.name: Saltmere
villages.why: On a sheltered creek of the east coast between Larkmouth and Lumeport, among salt meadows behind the shore, a few kilometres off the coast road.
villages.lives_on: The east coast's small harbour, fishing, salt-meadow lamb, the market of the coast's farms.

villages.name: Ternhaven
villages.why: At a creek mouth on the east coast, behind a spit where terns nest.
villages.lives_on: Fishing, sheep on the runs behind.

villages.name: Felulaka
villages.why: On a flat of old landslide debris at the foot of the west cliffs (a faja), reached by a track down the cliff.
villages.lives_on: Gardens, fruit and fishing.

villages.name: Nihekemo
villages.why: On the south-west coast where a stream falls from the cliffs to the shore.
villages.lives_on: Gardens and fishing.

villages.name: Setahu
villages.why: On the north coast west of the cotton plain, under a headland that keeps off the westerly swell: the last landing before the cliffs of the windward side.
villages.lives_on: Fishing, gardens below the forest.

villages.name: Linukaha
villages.why: At the mouth of the largest stream of the south coast, where two streams meet.
villages.lives_on: Fishing, gardens and cotton on the coastal flat.

villages.name: Natahoma
villages.why: In the most sheltered bay of the north coast, where a stream comes in.
villages.lives_on: Fishing and canoe building, gardens.

wiki.short: Fishing village on the north coast of Lisavu, the oldest settlement of the island
wiki.lead: **Natahoma** is a fishing village on the north coast of [[Lisavu]], with about {people} people, in the most sheltered bay of that coast. By the Lisavans' tradition the first canoes landed here, and its village sites, about 2,000 years old, are the oldest on the island.

sections.title: Geography
sections.text: The village lies at the head of the bay, where a stream comes in. Its Lisavan name means anchorage.

sections.title: History
sections.text: The Lisavans' tradition tells of ancestors who came over the sea by canoe and landed in this bay. From here villages spread along the island's sheltered coasts in the centuries after.

sections.title: Economy
sections.text: Natahoma lives from fishing, its gardens and the building of canoes, a craft the village has kept.

villages.name: Lintwell
villages.why: On the dry north-eastern plain on the road north of the town, at a well dug for an English settler's cotton estate.
villages.lives_on: Cotton.

villages.name: Bollworth
villages.why: On the coast of the cotton plain north of Selanu, where the estates landed their bales for the ships.
villages.lives_on: Cotton, fishing.

villages.name: Ontanella
villages.why: On a confluence in the western hills, among alder woods along the streams.
villages.lives_on: Mixed farming, alder and chestnut wood.

villages.name: Faggiorna
villages.why: High on the wet western hills, on a shelf below the beech woods where two streams meet.
villages.lives_on: Dairy cattle and hay meadows, beech wood and charcoal.

villages.name: Duefiumi
villages.why: Where two rivers of the western hills meet, a few kilometres from the coast.
villages.lives_on: The market and services of the wet west, dairy works, a small harbour at the river mouth.

districts.name: Ponte Vecchio
districts.note: The old town at the bridge where the two rivers meet.

districts.name: Corso Sardo
districts.note: The Sardinian and Italian main street with the court and the barracks.

districts.name: Duefiumi Mare
districts.note: Housing and the dairy works down the valley towards the coast.

villages.name: Fucinalta
villages.why: Just below Serravona on the road up from the valley, where iron ore came out of the hillsides and charcoal from the woods: the Urvanians' smithies (the iron that named Ferrano).
villages.lives_on: Mixed farming, chestnut woods, a forge that still makes tools.

villages.name: Gradinella
villages.why: On a terrace of the upper valley above the river's floodplain, at the foot of the slope, where springs rise.
villages.lives_on: Vineyards and orchards on terraced slopes, fields below.

villages.name: Castagnoro
villages.why: At a confluence in the hills south-west of Ferrano, among chestnut woods.
villages.lives_on: Chestnuts, small fields and meadows, pigs.

villages.name: Porto Riparo
villages.why: At the head of a long inlet on the north-west coast, the most sheltered anchorage of Urvania's coast, where a river comes in.
villages.lives_on: The north-west's harbour: fishing, fish processing, the coastal shipping, the market of the inlet's farms.

districts.name: Il Molo
districts.note: The fishermen's town round the harbour at the head of the inlet.

districts.name: Riparo Italiano
districts.note: The Italian naval station's quarter: quays, stores and the harbour office.

districts.name: Riparo Alto
districts.note: Housing on the hill above the harbour, the fish processing.

villages.name: San Ranieri del Guado
villages.founded: Tuscan, about 1611 (the friars' chapel); the Urvanian hamlet older
villages.why: At an old ford of the upper river, a day's walk above the rapids: friars of the Tuscan voyage of 1609-10 built a chapel to Pisa's saint beside the Urvanian hamlet at the ford; the chapel outlasted the trading post.
villages.lives_on: Fields on the valley floor, vineyards and orchards, a little pilgrimage to the chapel.

villages.name: Mandria Nova
villages.why: On the plain of a large river near the north coast, where an Italian land company settled farmers from the valley on a cattle estate.
villages.lives_on: Cattle and hay meadows, wheat.

villages.name: Portaggio
villages.why: At the head of the rapids above Ruldraz (Ferrano), where a large tributary joins the river: boats coming down from the upper valley were unloaded here and their loads carried round the rapids.
villages.lives_on: The market of the upper valley and its wine, food works, workshops; commuters to Ferrano.

districts.name: Borgo del Porto
districts.note: The Urvanian carters' and boatmen's village at the head of the rapids, round the landing.

districts.name: Via Nuova
districts.note: The Italian street to Ferrano along the portage road, with the church and the school.

districts.name: Quartiere della Diga
districts.note: Housing and workshops by the weir built across the tributary after independence.

villages.name: Pietramiglia
villages.founded: Urvanian, before 1600; named under Italian rule
villages.why: On the valley road from Ruldraz up to the hills of Serravona, beside the railway, at a stone the Sardinian road builders set at the tenth mile.
villages.lives_on: Brick works and workshops by the railway, the valley's farms; commuters to Ferrano.

districts.name: Pietramiglia Vecchia
districts.note: The Urvanian village on the valley road.

districts.name: La Stazione
districts.note: The station, the carters' yards and the brick works by the railway.

districts.name: Pietramiglia Nuova
districts.note: Houses for Ferrano's commuters along the valley road.

villages.name: Grancelle
villages.why: At the end of Ferrano's farm road south across the river bridge, where the grain of the southern hills was stored before it went down to the town.
villages.lives_on: Wheat and barley, the granaries, and Ferrano's commuters.

villages.name: Pomarella
villages.why: On the gentle slope above Ferrano's northern edge, on the road and the railway north, on well-drained ground facing the sun.
villages.lives_on: Orchards and market gardens for Ferrano's markets.

villages.name: Conciaro
villages.why: On a stream east of Ferrano, on the main road to the border: the hides of the cattle markets were tanned here, downwind of the town.
villages.lives_on: Farming, a leather works that grew from the tanneries.

villages.name: Salicora
villages.why: On the floodplain where two streams meet, among willows (cut for baskets and hurdles).
villages.lives_on: Wheat, willow-growing and baskets, sheep on the hills.

villages.name: Fierabruna
villages.why: Where two large rivers of the plateau meet north-east of Ferrano, on the drovers' way down from the hills: the old cattle fair of the region.
villages.lives_on: The cattle fair and the meat works, the market of the plateau's farms, schools and the hospital of the hills.

districts.name: La Fiera
districts.note: The old fair ground at the confluence and the lanes round it.

districts.name: Borgo Stazione
districts.note: The Italian quarter towards Ferrano: the cattle market's offices and the inns.

districts.name: Fierabruna Nuova
districts.note: Housing and the meat works on the terrace above the confluence.

villages.name: Fontebrina
villages.why: At the foot of the hills where springs rise along a line of harder rock, beside a confluence.
villages.lives_on: Wheat and sheep, the springs bottled since the Italian period.

villages.name: Lanternino
villages.founded: Urvanian, before 1600; the harbour light Italian, 1890s
villages.why: In a sheltered bay of the south coast, where the Italian administration put a harbour light and a jetty.
villages.lives_on: The south coast's fishing harbour and cannery, its market, summer visitors.

districts.name: Marina
districts.note: The fishermen's quarter round the old landing in the bay.

districts.name: Il Faro
districts.note: The Italian harbour works: the light, the jetty, the customs house and the promenade.

districts.name: Lanternino Alta
districts.note: Housing on the slope above the bay and the fish cannery.

villages.name: Forte Euridice
villages.founded: Sardinian, 1842 (the fort); the village after it
villages.why: On the north bank in the angle between the main river and the largest plateau river, just above their confluence, where the land border meets the river: the Sardinian protectorate built a fort here to watch the river and the British settlers beyond the plateau river, and named it after the corvette Euridice of its station on the Plata, which had first shown the flag on the river; the boundary convention of 1857 made that river and the watershed the border.
villages.lives_on: The border crossing: customs agents, hauliers and warehouses, the railway, the valley's farms.

districts.name: Il Forte
districts.note: The Sardinian fort in the angle of the two rivers and the garrison village round it.

districts.name: Borgo della Dogana
districts.note: The customs house and the traders' street that grew after the boundary convention.

districts.name: Forte Nuovo
districts.note: Warehouses, the hauliers and housing of the Accord's border trade.

villages.name: Vignacorta
villages.why: On the south bank of the lower valley, below a short, steep slope that faces north, to the sun.
villages.lives_on: Vineyards along the slope, fields on the floodplain.

villages.name: Saline Brune
villages.why: On a flat stretch of the south coast where a stream comes down to a lagoon: salt pans.
villages.lives_on: Salt, fishing, wheat and vines behind the shore.

villages.name: Torre Colombina
villages.why: At a stream mouth on the south coast, its farms known for their dovecotes.
villages.lives_on: Wheat, vines and olives, pigeons, fishing.

villages.name: Marina Ligure
villages.why: In a cove of the south coast where a stream comes down: Ligurian fishermen from the Sardinian kingdom's colony on the Plata settled here under the protectorate.
villages.lives_on: Fishing, boatbuilding, gardens behind the shore.

villages.name: Passobarca
villages.why: On the south shore of the estuary opposite Lumeport, where the ferry lands.
villages.lives_on: The ferry to Lumeport, fishing, market gardens for the capital across the water.

rivers_note: The names of the rivers the encyclopedia names (world/terrain.json, rivers: every stream whose basin reaches 1,000 km² on the mainland or 500 km² on Lisavu), matched by the river's mouth in squares. A river of Urvania has its Italian name, from the protectorate, and its Urvanian one (from the vocabulary, by the meaning in name_from), as the towns have; the main river keeps its Urvanian name in every language; a river of Bayvarra has the English name its settlers gave it, Lisavu's rivers their Lisavan names. A wiki key adds prose to the article the encyclopedia makes from the terrain.

wiki.short: Main river of the mainland, through Urvania and along the border to Lumeport
wiki.lead: The **Runmek** is the main river of the mainland, {km} km long, with a basin of {basin} km², about a third of the mainland. It rises on the volcanic massif of [[Urvania]] at about {source_m} m, runs through the rift valley past [[Ferrano]], forms the border with [[Bayvarra]] from Forte Euridice down, and reaches the sea by the estuary at [[Lumeport]]. Its name is Urvanian and means mother; the Italians and the British kept it.

sections.title: Course
sections.text: From the massif the river runs south-east through the rift valley, 15 to 18 km wide, and takes in the [[Nevola]] and the [[Castagna (river)|Castagna]]. Just above [[Ferrano]] it falls through rapids, from about 124 to 91 m in about 12 km, which end navigation: the barges work below them. At Forte Euridice the [[Bruna (river)|Bruna]], its largest tributary, joins it; from there to the estuary the river is the border, and the [[River Tallow|Tallow]] and the [[River Marrow|Marrow]] come in from Bayvarra's plateau.

sections.title: History
sections.text: The Urvanians' town, Ruldraz, now [[Ferrano]], grew where the valleys meet, below the rapids. In 1840 the Sardinian corvette *Euridice* sailed up the river to Ruldraz, and the boundary convention of 1857 made the river the border below the confluence, with free navigation to the sea.

wiki.short: River of Bayvarra's dry east, to the sea at Larkmouth
wiki.lead: The **Lark** is the largest river of [[Bayvarra]] and the second of the mainland, {km} km long, with a basin of {basin} km². It rises at about {source_m} m, crosses the dry east and reaches the sea at [[Larkmouth]], which is named after it.

sections.title: History
sections.text: The first British settlers landed at its mouth on 16 February 1824, behind the headland, where they found a sheltered harbour, fresh water and dry grazing land behind it. Larkmouth, the town they built there, was the colony's first capital.

wiki.short: Largest tributary of the Runmek, in Urvania
wiki.lead: The **Bruna** (Urvanian *Gekgan*, brown) is the largest tributary of the [[Runmek]], {km} km long, with a basin of {basin} km², and lies wholly in [[Urvania]]. It rises on the high ground at about {source_m} m and joins the Runmek at Forte Euridice, where the road crosses the border. Fierabruna, the market town of its valley, is named after it.

sections.title: History
sections.text: In 1842 the Sardinian protectorate built Forte Euridice in the angle between the Bruna and the Runmek, just above their confluence, to watch the river. By the boundary convention of 1857 the Bruna's whole valley stayed with Urvania: north of the confluence the border follows the watershed.

wiki.short: River of Bayvarra's north, to the north coast
wiki.lead: The **Shingle** is a river of [[Bayvarra]], {km} km long, with a basin of {basin} km². It rises at about {source_m} m and reaches the sea on the north coast at Shinglebeck, which is named after it.

wiki.short: River of Bayvarra's plateau, a tributary of the Runmek
wiki.lead: The **Tallow** is a river of [[Bayvarra]], {km} km long, with a basin of {basin} km², the largest of the plateau's rivers that join the [[Runmek]] below the border crossing. It rises at about {source_m} m. The village of Tallowford, where the old drove road down the valley forded it some 5 km above its mouth, is named after it.

wiki.short: River of Bayvarra's plateau, past Marrowdale to the Runmek
wiki.lead: The **Marrow** is a river of [[Bayvarra]], {km} km long, with a basin of {basin} km². It rises on the plateau at about {source_m} m, runs south through the dale that gave [[Marrowdale]] its name, and joins the [[Runmek]] above [[Lumeport]].

wiki.short: The rivers, basins and watersheds of the mainland and Lisavu
wiki.lead: The mainland drains to the sea by many rivers, of which {mainland_rivers} have a basin of 1,000 km² or more; Lisavu's streams are short and steep, and {lisavu_rivers} of them drain more than 500 km². The largest river is the [[Runmek]], {main_km} km long, whose basin of {main_basin} km² covers about {main_share} % of the mainland.

sections.title: The mainland
sections.text: The [[Runmek]] rises on the volcanic massif in Urvania's north-west at about {main_source_m} m and runs south-east through the rift valley to the estuary at [[Lumeport]]. Its tributaries come from the massif, from the plateau to the north-east and from the southern hills; the largest is the [[Bruna (river)|Bruna]], which joins it at Forte Euridice. From the massif the [[Pastora]] falls to the north coast and the [[Vallerna]] and the [[Grigiola]] to the west coast. Bayvarra's north drains to the north coast by the [[River Shingle|Shingle]], the [[River Brackwater|Brackwater]] and the [[River Scarrow|Scarrow]], its north-east by the [[River Sallow|Sallow]], and the dry east by the [[River Lark|Lark]], the second river of the mainland. The southern hills send only short rivers to the south coast, among them the [[Colomba (river)|Colomba]] and the [[Genovina]].

sections.title: Watersheds and the border
sections.text: North of the crossing at Forte Euridice the border between [[Urvania]] and [[Bayvarra]] follows the watershed: Urvania holds the basins of the rivers that join the [[Runmek]] at or above the crossing, the Bruna's whole valley among them, and of the north-western coast; Bayvarra holds the land that drains to the Runmek below the crossing, to the rest of the north coast and to the east. From the crossing down to the estuary the Runmek itself is the border.

sections.title: Lisavu
sections.text: The island's streams run outward from its volcano, short and steep. The [[Vokila (river)|Vokila]] drains the largest basin and reaches the north coast in the bay of [[Natahoma]]; the [[Makete (river)|Makete]], the longest, reaches the south coast at [[Linukaha]]; the [[Tapetu (river)|Tapetu]] falls from near the summit to the south-west coast at [[Nihekemo]]; the [[Kanipi (river)|Kanipi]] runs to the east coast north of [[Selanu]].
